text:
maya: Quick heads-up — hit a weird accuracy regression on the AWQ/INT8 run for llama-3-13b during the new bakeoff on H100 (CUDA 14.0). Eval suite shows ~4.2% drop in exact-match on our dev prompt set compared to fp16 baseline. No obvious tokenization differences.

jamie: ugh. any kernel errors in the logs? or just numeric delta? :thinking_face: @maya

maya: Numeric scatter. Logs show a bunch of cuBLASLt warnings and a few lines where TensorRT falls back to reference GEMM. I pasted the small tail: 
```
[2026-04-12 09:12:33] E TRT: cuBLASLt returned CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR for epilogue kernel
[2026-04-12 09:12:33] W TRT: falling back to reference GEMM (slower, potential numeric diff)
[2026-04-12 09:12:33] I TRITON: model instance llm_0: using fallback backend path
```

linus: fallback path could explain numeric drift. Did Triton/TensorRT compile with CUDA14-compatible cuBLASLt? We recently saw API/ABI mismatch with driver 535.x and CUDA 14.0 containers.

priya: also check quant backend config — per-channel vs per-tensor scaling can change round-off behavior and interact poorly with fallback kernels. Which AWQ quant params did you use?

maya: AWQ run used default pipeline we used in bakeoff: `awq --bits 8 --group-size 128 --per-channel` — same config as our baseline runs. Buckets look ok.

jamie: can you repro with pure vLLM (no Triton/TrtLLM) on same machine? if vLLM with cuBLASLt path produces same regression then it's not Triton-specific.

maya: Good call — I spun up a direct vLLM run on the same node. vLLM shows a smaller drift (~1%) and no fallback logs. TensorRT path is the only one with consistent ~4% hit.

linus: that points at TensorRT kernel implementation differences when using INT8 on H100 + CUDA14. We had a similar SES issue where nvrtc produced different PTX for compute 8.0 vs 9.0 targets. What compute capability are you targeting in trt build?

maya: trt server built with -arch=sm_90 (H100). Driver is 535.86. Newer Triton container we used is tritonserver:23.12 (CUDA14).

jamie: can you paste the trt server start command and the model config? maybe there's an auto-quant kernel selection override.

maya: start command: 
```bash
tritonserver --model-repository=/models/triton_repo --backend-config=tensorRT,allow_gpu_fallback=true --log-verbose=1
```
model config excerpt: 
```yaml
instance_group:
  kind: KIND_GPU
  count: 1
parameters:
  precision: "int8"
```

sasha: allow_gpu_fallback=true will intentionally let TRT use fallback kernels. try false. Also confirm TRITON_TENSORRT_ALLOW_FP16_REORDER env var — there are knob interactions that change fused epilogue math.

maya: set allow_gpu_fallback=false and re-ran — log shows no fallback, but now the server crashes intermittently with `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED` (different failure). stack: 
```
E TRT: cublasLtMatmul: CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
F TRT: aborting due to unrecoverable kernel error
```

priya: hmm. crash vs fallback — we need stable eval. Could be driver+runtime mismatch. What does `nvidia-smi` show?

maya: nvidia-smi: 
```
NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 14.0
GPU 0: NVIDIA H100-SXM2-80GB 
```

linus: driver 535.86 + CUDA14 container is borderline. For TRT we usually run driver 535.104+ with CUDA14.1 or use CUDA13.6 for more maturity. Suggest two experiments: (1) pin to the tritonserver:23.10 (CUDA13) container, (2) rebuild TensorRT-LLM with CUDA14.1 toolchain and target sm_90 and run the same AWQ INT8 model.

jamie: also try switching quant group-size to 64 or 256 to see sensitivity — numeric rounding sometimes depends on accumulation window. low-effort check.

maya: I did a quick run with group-size 64 on Triton+TRT and the EM loss reduced to ~2.1% — so group-size matters. That suggests accumulation/scale interplay with kernel math.

priya: ok, immediate triage plan:
- maya: repro on A100 (to see if H100-specific) and run vLLM baseline (in progress)
- linus: build TRT-LLM against CUDA14.1 + cuBLASLt pinned and try server build
- jamie: run container downgrade test (tritonserver:23.10 CUDA13) and a config sweep on group-size [64,128,256]
- sasha: check model exporter to ensure quant params persisted (no accidental fp16 override)

sasha: small note — deploy-bot posted a recent infra change: `kernel-headers` updated on 2026-04-11 which bumped the host distro's libstdc++. That created an ABI edge with some older TRT builds. Might be related.

deploy-bot: Infra note: rolling back kernel-headers on h100-nodes is scheduled if reproducible test fails. Opened ticket INFRA-9223.

maya: thanks team. I'll attach the eval logs + the tiny failing prompt set to the ticket. If anyone wants to grab the node, it's h100-node-12 (reserved for our experiments).

jamie: if linus can build a quick TRT-LLM dev image I can run it on h100-node-12 tonight. Will report results tomorrow. :thumbsup:

linus: I can try. If it still fails with CUDA14.1 build then we escalate to Nvidia support with the kernel traces.

priya: perfect. goal: identify whether this is a numeric difference from fallback/reference kernels or a bug in TRT int8 epilogue for H100. Keep notes in the ticket and add the small eval diff set.

maya: added eval diff, logs, and seeds to INFRA-9223. Will update after A100 test completes (ETA 4hrs).
